questions.question: Compare questionnaires and interviews, evaluating strengths and limitations of each.

points.text: Questionnaires: large samples, cheap, anonymous (strengths); low response, social desirability, inflexible (limitations). Interviews: depth, follow-ups (strengths); interviewer bias, small samples (limitations).

questions.question: Explain why a sociologist might choose participant observation, and evaluate its ethical implications.

points.text: Participant observation: useful for deviant/closed groups. Ethical issues: covert = deception (violates consent) but may be only way to access some groups; overt = honest but Hawthorne effect.

questions.question: A researcher wants to study whether employers discriminate against ethnic minority applicants. Which method is most appropriate?

points.text: A field experiment (CV study like Wood's): send identical CVs varying only ethnic name. Tests actual behaviour, high ecological validity, can establish causation. Ethical issue: deception of employers.
